description: In routes/login.ts (login handler, line 34) the email field from the POST body is interpolated into a raw Sequelize query: SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '${req.body.email || ''}' AND password = '${security.hash(req.body.password || '')}' AND deletedAt IS NULL. models.sequelize.query() is called with no bind parameters. An email value of "' OR 1=1--" bypasses authentication and returns the first user row (typically the admin account).

In frontend/src/app/search-result/search-result.component.ts (filterTable, line 143) the URL query parameter q is passed to DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml() and stored in this.searchValue, which the template renders as HTML. Because bypassSecurityTrustHtml turns off Angular's XSS sanitizer, a crafted /#/search?q= link executes in the visitor's browser.
